items.title: Python Language Summit 2026
items.excerpt: The 2026 Python Language Summit was hosted in Kraków, Poland as part of EuroPython 2026. There were 15 talks covering free-threading, Rust, garbage collection, type annotations, and more.

items.title: Lightning Talks (Python Language Summit 2026)
items.excerpt: Lightning talks on a one-time ABI break, safer interruptions, EktuPy (Scratch but Python), an AGENTS.md file for CPython, and a call to read PEP 836.

items.title: PEP 827: Type Manipulation (Python Language Summit 2026)
items.excerpt: Michael J. Sullivan presents PEP 827 and discusses a key design decision: how to store type annotations?

items.title: Free-Threaded Python Post-Era (Python Language Summit 2026)
items.excerpt: Tobias Wrigstad, Fridtjof Stoldt, and Donghee Na propose a safe and performant, high-level concurrency model for free-threaded Python

items.title: Developer-in-Residence Update & Future (Python Language Summit 2026)
items.excerpt: Petr Viktorin gives an update on the Developer-in-Residence role and asks Python core developers for projects to prioritize

items.title: Spicycrab (Python Language Summit 2026)
items.excerpt: Kushal Das shows off Spicycrab, a Python-to-Rust transpiler for Python users who need performance without learning Rust or leaving Python

items.title: Rust for CPython (Python Language Summit 2026)
items.excerpt: David Hewitt shares a status update, first module, and potential acceptance criteria for the Rust for CPython project

items.title: Memory Snapshots for CPython (Python Language Summit 2026)
items.excerpt: Hood Chatham proposes memory snapshots and an initialization phase for speedier Python startups

items.title: Memory Buffer Protocol (Python Language Summit 2026)
items.excerpt: Nathan Goldbaum proposes safe concurrent access through buffer leases and custom data types for the Python Buffer Protocol.

items.title: Garbage Collection: Generational? Incremental? Both! (Python Language Summit 2026)
items.excerpt: Mark Shannon proposes a future garbage collection strategy for Python following the revert of the incremental garbage collector in Python 3.14

items.title: macOS and Python (Python Language Summit 2026)
items.excerpt: Ned Deily weighs whether Python should continue shipping macOS installers

items.title: One namespace to namespace them all (Python Language Summit 2026)
items.excerpt: Pablo Galindo Salgado proposes a top-level `std` namespace for the Python standard library to prevent module shadowing and free up module names.

briefing.executive_summary: O panorama de 2026 destaca avanços significativos em RPA, IA e automação de processos. UiPath consolida posição de liderança no Gartner, enquanto a comunidade Python celebra a liberação final da 3.15.0. Automation Anywhere continua a promover a integração de RPA e IA, com guias práticos e novos recursos como o Delegate. Novas iniciativas de IA, como o Playground da Google, ampliam as possibilidades de criação e experimentação.
